row.evidence: Pipedrive's plan comparison lists 'SAML SSO (single sign-on) login' on every plan and no SCIM or provisioning row; its help centre covers SSO with Okta and Entra ID only, and the Okta app is SAML/SWA only.
row.notes: Status changed from gated (June: SCIM on Ultimate, $79/seat/mo) to none by absence: no first-party page mentions SCIM. The June Ultimate SCIM claim has no first-party source and is dropped. Searched the pricing comparison table, the help-centre sitemap (568 articles; SSO, Okta and Entra SSO articles, no SCIM/provisioning article), the developer llms.txt index and the v1 OpenAPI spec. SAML SSO is on all plans (Lite $14, Growth $39, Premium $59, Ultimate $79 per seat/mo annual, unchanged since June). Okta OIN app is SAML + SWA; Entra and JumpCloud are SSO tutorials only. The REST API (all plans) can create users and toggle active_flag, but no IdP connector uses it.

plans.name: Ultimate
plans.notes: Comparison table shows 'Device history and audit log' only on Ultimate (UI feature; no audit-log API documented).

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint, SCIM article or SCIM pricing row found on any first-party page; left null (absence, not a vendor 'no').

user_api.notes: API access is ticked on all four plans in the pricing comparison (icon); daily token budget scales with plan multiplier and seats.

capabilities.notes: PUT /users/{id} only updates active_flag, so profile updates are not possible; deactivate/reactivate via active_flag.

events: user (Webhooks v2 event object: Users in your company)

rate_limits.text: Token-based daily budget per company: 30,000 base tokens x plan multiplier x seats (+ top-ups); each endpoint has a token cost.

limitations.text: User update via API is limited to active_flag.

okta.notes: OIN capability icons show SAML and SWA only (no provisioning; icons not quotable).

entra.notes: Microsoft Learn has an SSO tutorial; no Pipedrive provisioning tutorial (pipedrive-provisioning-tutorial returns 404).

jumpcloud.notes: JumpCloud SAML SSO connector article; no provisioning described.

fallbacks.notes: SSO article says users set up in the IdP 'automatically have login credentials', but does not clearly describe JIT account creation; left null.
